title: Goodwill Share of the Validation-Wait Credit
content:
SSL/TLS Certificates — basis questions on goodwill already granted for a delayed certificate.

**Rule.** Where the customer's Harborline Customer Accounts credit ledger shows goodwill credit granted for the subscription, the validation-wait credit of that multi-domain subscription keeps only a goodwill share of its days:

- goodwill totalling 25.00 USD or more leaves a share of 0 percent (the credit keeps none of its days);
- goodwill above zero but below 25.00 USD leaves a share of 40 percent;
- without such goodwill, the credit keeps all its days.

**Which ledger entries count as goodwill for the subscription?**
Goodwill credit entries in the account credit ledger whose source category is SSL and whose source charge reference is the subscription's purchase order number (the Harborline order number on its new-subscription line). Goodwill entries for another subscription, another order number or another product category do not count.

**Is the goodwill judged entry by entry?**
No. The amounts of all qualifying goodwill entries for the subscription are taken together, and the total decides the share.

**Where exactly are the edges?**

| Goodwill total for the subscription | Share of its days the validation-wait credit keeps |
|---|---|
| none recorded | all its days |
| 0.01 to 24.99 USD | 40 percent |
| 25.00 USD | 0 percent |
| more than 25.00 USD | 0 percent |

**Hypothetical illustration.** An invented subscription with a validation-wait credit of 45 days has two goodwill entries of 6.50 USD and 11.75 USD against its purchase order number, 18.25 USD in all. That total is below 25.00 USD, so the credit keeps 40 percent of its days: 18 days. Had a further entry of 7.00 USD been recorded against the same order number, the total of 25.25 USD would leave a share of 0 percent.
